transcript.heading: News Report One (British Female)
paras: A major heat wave is sweeping across Southern Europe, with temperatures exceeding 45 degrees Celsius in parts of Spain, Italy, and Greece. Authorities have issued red alerts in several regions, urging residents to stay indoors and drink plenty of water. The extreme weather has forced the closure of tourist sites, including the Acropolis in Athens during midday hours. Hospitals have reported a significant increase in patients suffering from heat-related illnesses. Meteorologists say the heat wave is being caused by a high-pressure system from North Africa and could last for another week. Several countries have opened public cooling centers in libraries, community centers, and shopping malls to help people without air conditioning escape the extreme heat.
Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.

2. Why has the Acropolis been closed during midday hours?

transcript.heading: News Report Two (American Male)
paras: The Walt Disney Company has announced plans to become completely carbon neutral by 2030. The entertainment giant says it will reduce direct emissions by 50% from 2019 levels, invest in renewable energy projects, and implement sustainable design practices across all its theme parks and facilities worldwide. Disney also plans to eliminate single-use plastics from all its resorts and cruise ships by 2025. The company currently operates 12 theme parks across the globe, along with a cruise line and numerous hotels. Environmental groups have praised the announcement, though some critics say the targets are not ambitious enough given the company's environmental impact. Disney has already reduced its emissions by 17% since 2019 through solar power installations and energy efficiency upgrades.
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.

4. What has Disney already achieved since 2019?

transcript.heading: News Report Three (British Male)
paras: Researchers at the University of Oxford have developed a new malaria vaccine that has shown 77% effectiveness in large-scale clinical trials. The vaccine, called R21/Matrix-M, was tested on over 450 children in Burkina Faso over a 12-month period. If approved by the World Health Organization, it would become the first highly effective vaccine against malaria, a disease that kills over 400,000 people annually, most of them young children in Africa. The research team is now working with manufacturers to produce over 200 million doses annually at affordable prices for low-income countries. Health officials describe the development as a historic breakthrough in the fight against one of the world's deadliest infectious diseases. The vaccine is expected to be available for distribution as early as next year.
Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
5. What have researchers at Oxford developed?
6. How effective was the vaccine in clinical trials?

transcript.heading: Conversation One (American Female + American Male)
paras: Woman (Lisa): Hi James, did you find an apartment yet for next semester?
Man (James): Not yet, Lisa. It's been really stressful. All the good places close to campus are either too expensive or already taken.
Woman: I know, the housing market is terrible this year. Have you checked the university's off-campus housing website?
Man: Yeah, I check it every day. Most of the listings are either for shared rooms in houses or way over my budget. I'm trying to stay under $800 a month.
Woman: Wait, my roommate is graduating early, so her room will be available starting in August. Would you be interested in seeing it?
Man: That sounds great! Where is your apartment?
Woman: It's on Oak Street, just a 10-minute walk from the main library. It's a two-bedroom apartment with a kitchen, living room, and a small balcony.
Man: That's really close to campus! How much is the rent?
Woman: Her half is $750 a month, which includes water and internet. We split the electricity bill, which is usually about $50 each.
Man: That's within my budget! Can I come see it tomorrow afternoon?
Woman: Sure, I have classes until 3 PM, so anytime after 4 would work. I'll text you the address.
Man: Perfect! Thanks so much, Lisa. You're a lifesaver.

paras: Man: Welcome to Riverside Restaurant. Do you have a reservation?

Man: Absolutely, here are the menus. We have several vegetarian dishes, including a mushroom risotto and a vegetable curry. We also have vegan options if you need them.
Woman: Great, thank you. My friend is a vegetarian, so that's good to know. Could we also order some drinks at the bar while we wait?
Man: Of course. The bartender will be right with you. Let me just note your name...?

Man: Thank you, Ms. Thompson. I'll come find you when your table is ready. Would you prefer indoor or outdoor seating?

transcript.heading: Passage One (American Female)
paras: The Great Wall of China is one of the most famous structures in the world, stretching over 13,000 miles across northern China. Contrary to popular belief, the Great Wall is not a single continuous wall but a series of walls and fortifications built by different dynasties over a period of more than 2,000 years. Construction first began in the 7th century BC, with the most well-known sections built during the Ming Dynasty between the 14th and 17th centuries. The wall was originally built to protect Chinese states from invasions by nomadic tribes from the north. Today, the Great Wall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of China's most popular tourist attractions, drawing millions of visitors each year. However, many sections of the wall are in disrepair due to natural erosion and human damage, and conservation efforts are underway to preserve this iconic monument for future generations.

transcript.heading: Passage Two (British Female)
paras: Color psychology is the study of how colors affect human behavior, mood, and emotions. While reactions to color can be somewhat personal and influenced by cultural background, researchers have found some general patterns. Blue, for example, is often associated with calmness and trust, which is why many banks and financial institutions use blue in their logos and branding. Red is linked to excitement, energy, and urgency, making it a popular choice for sale signs and fast-food restaurants. Green represents nature, growth, and health, and is frequently used by organic food companies and environmental organizations. Yellow is considered optimistic and attention-grabbing, though it can also cause eye fatigue in large amounts. Businesses carefully choose colors for their brands and products based on these psychological effects to influence how customers perceive them and behave.
Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.

20. Why do many banks use blue in their branding?

transcript.heading: Passage Three (American Male)
paras: The concept of a four-day work week has gained significant attention in recent years as companies explore ways to improve employee well-being and productivity. Instead of the traditional five-day, 40-hour work week, employees work four days, typically 32 hours, while receiving the same pay and benefits. Several large-scale trials have been conducted around the world, including a major study in the United Kingdom involving 61 companies and over 2,900 workers. The results were overwhelmingly positive: 39% of employees reported feeling less stressed, 71% reported reduced levels of burnout, and productivity remained stable or even improved at most companies. Nearly all participating companies decided to continue with the four-day arrangement after the trial ended. Proponents argue that shorter work weeks lead to better work-life balance, improved mental health, lower absenteeism, and higher employee retention. Critics, however, raise concerns about whether the model works for all industries and whether it could lead to increased pressure on workers during the four days they are on the job.
